prompt: Write 10 distinct short extracts of Larkmere Mutual's official guidance, procedures or policy wording about: self-employed income evidence. Two to four sentences each, in the society's own formal voice. Use type "fact". Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"Where an applicant is self-employed, Larkmere Mutual will normally ask for the latest two years of SA302 calculations and corresponding tax year overviews. If trading through a limited company, we may also request full company accounts and the most recent business bank statements. Additional evidence may be required where income has varied materially year on year."},{"type":"fact","content":"Self-employed income must be evidenced from documents that are consistent with the declared figures on the application. We will not rely solely on a verbal declaration of expected earnings. If the available evidence does not support affordability, the application may be referred for manual review."},{"type":"fact","content":"For sole traders, net profit is generally assessed after allowable business expenses and before personal drawings. For partners, we will consider the applicant’s share of the partnership profits as shown in the relevant accounts or tax documentation. We may average income over a suitable period where trading results are seasonal or irregular."},{"type":"fact","content":"Where the applicant has been self-employed for less than two full years, Larkmere Mutual may accept a shorter trading history if supported by strong evidence of continuity. This may include an accountant’s reference, current year management information and evidence of prior experience in the same trade. Approval remains subject to our underwriting criteria."},{"type":"fact","content":"We may ask for business bank statements to confirm that self-employed income is received regularly and that the business remains active. Statements should normally cover the most recent three to six months. Large unexplained credits or debits may require further explanation before a decision is made."},{"type":"fact","content":"Income that is drawn from a company by salary and dividends must be supported by payslips, dividend vouchers and company accounts where applicable. We will consider the sustainable level of income, not one-off distributions that cannot reasonably be maintained. If dividends have fallen in the current year, we may use the lower figure for assessment."},{"type":"fact","content":"Where tax documentation is unavailable, the applicant must provide alternative evidence acceptable to Larkmere Mutual. Such evidence may include certified accounts, an accountant’s letter on headed paper, or HMRC correspondence confirming declared income. We reserve the right to decline any evidence that is incomplete, inconsistent or not independently verifiable."},{"type":"fact","content":"Projected future income will only be considered where there is a clear and credible basis for the projection. We will base our assessment primarily on historical evidence and current trading performance."},{"type":"fact","content":"If self-employed income fluctuates significantly, we may apply an average across the most recent available years to establish a representative figure. In some cases, we may exclude an abnormal year if there is a documented reason such as illness, maternity, market disruption or a one-off contract loss. The final assessment will be made at Larkmere Mutual’s discretion."},{"type":"fact","content":"Applicants must disclose all sources of self-employed income, including consultancy fees, freelance work, commissions and rental income from business property where relevant.
